clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. EO 6885-A (October 25, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) incorporates by reference the annexed report of the National Industrial Recovery Board, finds that the amended code complies with Title I, orders 'that the Code as amended be and it is hereby approved' and modifies 'the previous approval of said Code ... to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended' (the Builders Supplies Trade code). The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6885A is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6885-amended-code-fair-competition-for-the-builders-supplies-trade.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (ee86cd5cea00...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-47, captured 2025-11-14T21:11:16Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6885-A—Amended Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade' and whose date is 1934-10-25; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('Oct 25, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6885-A—Amended Code of Fair Competition for the Builders Supplies Trade', 1934-10-25) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 594: 'Amendments to Code of Fair Competition for the Build ers Supplies Trade approved. XVIII NRA Codes 313.'). The WPA list adds the citation XVIII NRA Codes 313. EO 6885-A (October 25, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) incorporates by reference the annexed report of the National Industrial Recovery Board, finds that the amended code complies with Title I, orders 'that the Code as amended be and it is hereby approved' and modifies 'the previous approval of said Code ... to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as amended' (the Builders Supplies Trade code). Legal reading: a section 3(a) approval of a code of fair competition with no period, condition or exception of its own; its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I and ended with the repeal of the approval and enforcement provisions on 1935-06-14 (Senate Joint Resolution 113, section 2), unless an earlier end appears. No earlier end was found (see the earlier-end check). 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end: the order states no period, condition, 'until' date, 'pending' clause or provisional approval; its only operative command is the approval. The name search found one other order naming this code, EO 6312 of October 3, 1933, the earlier approval that this order modifies; an amendment of a code is a later event of the earlier approval, not an end of this order. No later held order names the code. Searches made on 2026-10-29: (1) a full-text search of every held order text numbered 6200 through 7100 under jobs/*/output/texts (APP, HathiTrust GPO, Wikisource and Federal Register texts; clause-drafts copies excluded) for the code's name; (2) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number; (3) a search of the same texts for general NRA orders that could suspend, cancel or supersede codes: the held general orders (EO 6354 as amended by EO 6710, EO 6646, 6711, 6750-C, 6764 and 6829) prescribe rules, contract terms and delegations, and none suspends, cancels or supersedes the code named here; (4) the census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list, read for this code's name; they show no cancellation, suspension or superseding code. Orders for which no text is held (for example EO 6454) could not be searched, so the search covers held texts only. No held record shows this code cancelled or modified under section 10(b), superseded by another code, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: it was Title I's original two-year expiry under section 2(c), which section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced with April 1, 1936. The approved code's own text is not held (it is printed in the NRA Codes volumes the WPA list cites), so a code-internal expiry or effective-date term could not be read; no held order records one for this code. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, May 27, 1935) is recorded in source_notes as a validity characterization, not as an end date: it reversed one conviction and held the Live Poultry Code provisions invalid, it did not cancel or withdraw this approving order, and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on that date.","independent_command_check":"The order contains one command, the approval. It appoints no one, creates no body, delegates nothing under another statute and directs no agency. The recital that the Board 'rendered their report' is not a command to the Board.","savings_check":"Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. This order states no savings or continuing clause of its own.","scope_check":"The inventory is one clause, the operative paragraph beginning 'Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt' that adopts the Administrator's report and approves the code; the machine inventory is correct and is confirmed. The recital before it states the statutory findings on which the approval rests; the signature, the 'Approval recommended' line and the date line command nothing. The annexed report of the Board that the order incorporates by reference is not part of the held text; the operative command is the approval, and no condition, stay or exception appears in the order's own words. The approval is a single act of one scope; no partial event reaching only part of it was found."}

savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. This order states no savings or continuing clause of its own.

source_notes.reason: Schechter, 295 U.S. 495: the judgment holds the code provisions in question invalid and reverses the conviction in No. 854; recorded with the syllabus and the delegation passage as a validity characterization of every section 3 code approval, not as an end date.

source_notes.reason: Schechter opinion: 'We think that the code-making authority thus conferred is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power.' The holding reaches section 3 approvals generally; it cancelled or withdrew no approving order.

source_notes.date_qualification: No event date: statutory text of June 16, 1933; the provisions delegating approval power and providing for code enforcement were repealed June 14, 1935.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 3(a)-(f): the legal effects of a code approval that the repeal removed (3(a) approval and conditions, 3(b) standards of fair competition, 3(c) injunction suits, 3(f) misdemeanor).

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-06-16: not an end; section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced this expiry with April 1, 1936.
source_notes.reason: NIRA section 2(c): Title I's original two-year expiry, which fell on June 16, 1935.
